title: A Probabilistic HLbC–IGTC Framework for Predictive Semantics, Grammar Expansion, and Catastrophe-Type Cognitive Transitions
content: This study extends the normalized five-stage stochastic architecture of Human Language-based Consciousness (HLbC) with an optional grammar-update kernel. We use Information-Geometric Theory of Creativity (IGTC) to denote the extension developed here. The framework distinguishes task performance, subjective insight, and externally attributed consciousness. For finite controlled prediction tasks, we establish the coarsest predictive partition, the minimal additional alphabet preserving an existing representation, and a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for reconstructing predictive states from available recognition and memory. Under Bayes-optimal log loss, the value of an added feature equals conditional mutual information; restricted prediction families introduce explicit approximation terms. A KL-regularized objective yields a normalized grammar-proposal posterior. Its true-rule mass is proved to be a submartingale under a fixed supported model, correct likelihoods, a declared action policy, and cumulative evidence. Explicit scalar and two-state recognition models give conditional instability and fold criteria. A finite-state reset process supplies the scalar mean-field limit, while retaining a unique stationary distribution at each finite population size. Exact enumeration shows that finite-budget exploration rankings depend on prior mass, noise, query order, and the chosen objective. Published aggregates from 546 participants in two card-sorting experiments are independently recomputed and show discordance between reported rules and self-reported Aha. These aggregates do not identify latent grammar-generation events, cognitive bifurcations, or full-group Aha prevalence when non-solver reports are unavailable. The contribution is a mathematically specified, falsifiable synthesis with distinct assumptions, proofs, numerical illustrations, and empirical limitations.
